messages.author: b4c7251dafd737c8
messages.subject: Fwd: Question about the font of the axis labels and titles in ggplot2
parts:
Hello,


I use the following code to produce the graph attached:

ggplot(tab3$int,aes(x=Package,y=B,colour=Package,shape=factor(mu)),size=4)+geom_point()+

theme_bw()+opts(panel.margin=unit(0,"lines"))+ scale_shape_manual("Marginal mean", values = c(1, 4)) +

labs(y="Intercept Bias")+ ylim(-1.5,1.5)+ geom_point(size=3)+facet_grid(overdispersion~N+offset,labeller=label_both)+

geom_hline(yintercept=0,colour="gray",linetype=2)


Could anyone tell me, please, how to increase the font of the axis labels and titles. For other figures, I use arguments cex.axis and/or cex.lab, but with ggplot2 I don't know how to achieve that. 

Thank you very much!


Martí

Marti,

 

You can use something like this:

 

opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size = 16), axis.text.y = theme_text(size = 16),

        axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 16), axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 16, angle = 90)

 

 

Steve

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Question about the font of the axis labels and titles in ggplot2
parts:
In versions of ggplot2 >= 0.9.2, opts() is deprecated and replaced by
theme(). In a similar vein, theme_*() is replaced by element_*(), so
the following should work for more recent versions:

theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 16),
axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
axis.title.y = element_text(angle = 90))

The above is an abridged version of the previously offered solution
because the new theming system supports inheritance of properties of
theme elements. Thus, changes to axis.text propagate to axis.text.x
and axis.text.y, for example.

Dennis
